original_card.question: Can a decoder deliver the local paid mass in fewer, larger-rank children (block frame climbs instead of rank-1 to rank-3 steps)?
methods: Find one exact small decoding identity whose frame path climbs in blocks, and price its complete per-call profile.
Bound the best effective child rank achievable for one fixed support alphabet, including copies, frames and restoration.
original_card.acceptance_gate: A per-call local profile, with all copied information, frames and restoration counted, whose ceiling exceeds the selected word's by at least 5%; masked or overcomplete supports must change an assumption of the eight-term all-pairs bound.

first_step.inspect: Read the selected word's per-call local profile, its packing ceiling and the lever table; run levers.py for the ideal budget of the lever you target.
first_step.scope: Positive control and planning budget only; this is not a new construction or full cold replay.

original_card.first_experiment: Before any synthesis, write the candidate per-call local profile (and centre charge / unpaid coordinates if changed) and screen it with ceiling.ceiling(); reject it if even the ideal ceiling does not beat the selected word's by your stated margin. Ideal budget: rank-16 delivery is 2.31x (levers.py).
original_card.bottleneck_link: Rank-1 children are about half of recursive cost; the selected word's effective child rank is about 3.9. Larger-rank delivery lowers recursive cost per unit of paid mass.
allowed_variations: One masked, overcomplete or block decoder family with exact labels and supports.
A scoped lower bound on effective rank for one alphabet.
If the coverage law, template or guard changes, derive an applicable fully charged replacement bound instead of applying the incumbent ceiling outside its scope.
scope_change_triggers: Repacking idle remainders of an unchanged word (covered by the packing ceiling).
Repeating the eight-term all-pairs search inside its proved scope.

actual_scope: In the abstract Eisenstein E8 scalar binary decoder model of research/eisenstein-clique-copy-bound (PR798; optimum known in [22,40], clique certificates provably stop at 22), do rank bounds on non-clique principal submatrices of the fitting pattern lift the copy floor above 22?
scope_change_reason: The card's diagonal-batch line is closed by PR679 and the diagonal-child-contract audit, and its live variants are claimed by other contributors. This decoder floor is the copy-cost side of the same card ('a scoped lower bound for one alphabet'): PR1794 shows an Eisenstein supplier beats the selected record only if C <= 31, and DreamingOfClouds' discussion-1167 note names it one of the sharper open decoder targets.
bottleneck_link: Side result on an alternative complex unit: narrows PR1794's necessary window for an Eisenstein supplier from C in 22..31 to 23..31. No supplier, kappa or selected-record change.
stop_rule: Stop after an exact certificate for the first integer above 22, plus a class-level exploration of whether principal-submatrix sets can go further; no decoder construction.
evidence: verify.py (stdlib, exact): imports PR798's pinned geometry; exhaustive normalized search shows the 18-line core of S_uw = N[u] & N[w] has no fitting completion of rank <= 7 (rank-8 witness rebuilt), so minrank(S_uw) = 10 vs clique-dual price 9.5; five pinned automorphisms are transitive on the 540 nonorthogonal pairs; weights 184/6835, 13/13670, 7/20505 satisfy all 296,321 positive-cost flat-pair inequalities (601 tight); objective 30200/1367 > 22 so C >= 23; 5 rejection controls; RESULT.json pinned. Exploration (not replayed): class-uniform LP over 78 classes of hit-maximal sets also gives 30200/1367.
author: Josie Elliston
ai_assistance: Claude Code (Claude Opus 5.5) did the search, proof and verifier under the author's direction; one OpenAI Codex read-only review. Exploration used python-sat, networkx and scipy in a private venv; the replay is stdlib only.

open_questions.question: Is 30200/1367 the exact limit of principal-submatrix certificates?
open_questions.why_it_matters: Tells the next prover whether more set families can help or a new ingredient is required.
open_questions.first_step: Check that the 78 hit-maximal classes are automorphism orbits (or give per-class rank witnesses) and exhibit the matching dual.

open_questions.question: Can a cost-aware argument (like the Gaussian planar theorem) lift the bound past 23 on the 12-line Eisenstein hyperplanes?
open_questions.why_it_matters: The tight dual pairs are twelve-line hyperplane pairs; a bound >= 32 would close PR1794's window.
open_questions.first_step: Restrict to totals whose joint support has K-rank <= 3 and adapt the planar matching argument.
open_questions.blocked_by: Eisenstein planes hold up to four lines, so the matching step changes.

open_questions.question: Is there any fitting decoder cheaper than 40 (non-clean supports, C <= 31)?
open_questions.why_it_matters: Tests PR1794's remaining window from the upper side.
open_questions.first_step: SAT/ILP over flat-pair rectangles with parity constraints at cost <= 31.
open_questions.blocked_by: Parity constraints make LP relaxations weak; needs a good encoding.
